title: One slow click, recorded in a trace
purpose: See how a Performance recording shows a slow click as a long task on the main thread.
sequence_reason: Recording, the task and the red mark happen in order, and each step depends on the step before.
summary: You open the Performance panel, set CPU throttling, record while you click a button, and stop. The Main track shows the click handler as a task. In this example the handler needs 40 ms, 160 ms at 4x and 240 ms at 6x. A task over 50 ms is a long task: DevTools adds a red triangle and shades the time past 50 ms.
explanation: A trace turns a slow feeling into one task you can measure. The 50 ms limit tells you which tasks block the page.

learning_check.question: A task lasts 160 ms. Is it a long task, and how much of it is red?
learning_check.answer: Yes. It is over 50 ms, so DevTools marks it and shades the last 110 ms red.

scenes.heading: One slow click, recorded
scenes.narration: A button click feels slow. The Performance panel records a trace, so you can see the slow task.

visual.subtitle: Record, find the long task, explain the delay

scenes.heading: Record a runtime trace
scenes.narration: Open the Performance panel. Set CPU throttling. Click Record, click the button, then click Stop. The Main track shows the tasks.

items: Click Record, then click the button
Click Stop and read the Main track

scenes.heading: The click becomes a task
scenes.narration: The click starts a task on the main thread. The main thread runs one task at a time, so the next paint waits.

scenes.heading: Throttling slows the same work
scenes.narration: In this example the handler needs 40 milliseconds. A 4x slowdown makes it 160, and 6x makes it 240.

scenes.heading: Over 50 ms is a long task
scenes.narration: Any task over 50 milliseconds is a long task. DevTools adds a red triangle and shades only the time past 50 milliseconds red.

visual.verdict: A 160 ms task: the last 110 ms are red.
